To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Tbx-2, Tbx-3, Tbx-4, and Tbx- -5 chick genes have limb-specific expression patterns, and that Tbx-4 may be the gene that encodes legness.
the Tbx-2 to Tbx-5 genes are expressed in the chick limb regions and that their expression patterns are consistent with their involvement in determining limb identity.

(i) Tbx-4 expression is necessary and sufficient for leg identity, (ii) Tbx-5 is necessary and sufficient (with Tbx-3) for wing identity, (iii) Tbx-3 is necessary for limb identity, and (iv) Tbx-2 is necessary for flank identity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the development of the vertebrate limb.
the molecular basis of the development of the vertebrate limb and the evolution of the limb.
the role of T-box genes in limb formation and their potential as markers for the specification of wing versus leg identity in the developing limb.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Tbx genes, Tbx-2 to Tbx-5 have been shown to be involved in limb specification.
Tbx-4 encodes 'legness' and Tbx-2 encodes 'wingness', and that Tbx-2 is a target of the FGF signalling system.
the Tbx-2/3/4/5 genes are expressed in a pattern that correlates with the identity of the limb and that the expression of these genes is stable in the grafted limb bud tissue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Tbx genes are involved in limb identity and that Tbx-5 and Tbx-2 are involved in wing identity, and that Tbx4 and Tbx3 are involved in leg identity.

the expression patterns of the Tbx genes are very similar to those of the Hox genes, but the Tbx genes seem to act as selectors for the type of appendages that will form rather than specifying their proximo-distal and antero-posterior identities.
Tbx-4 expression in the limb bud is required for leg identity, whereas Tbx-5 is required for wing identity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the T-box genes Tbx-4 (in leg) and Tbx-2 (in wing) are expressed in the posterior and anterior regions of both wing and leg, and T-box genes Tbf-5 (in wing) and Tbx4 (in leg), are expressed only in one of the two limb regions.
Tbx-4 expression is necessary and sufficient for leg identity, whereas Tbx-5 is necessary and sufficient to specify the anterior wing.
the expression of T-box genes is not only important in the determination and patterning of limbs but also in the determination of limb identity.
